title: Working Out the Charge an Employee Carries to Their Pay
content:
What an employee consents to have carried to their pay for the meals they have charged at the counter on an Employee Meal Account is worked out from the account's own ledger, and the employee gives that consent themselves because it is their pay packet that meets it.

## 1. The meals carried

The meals carried are every meal rung against payroll on the account to date.

## 2. Allowance

No allowance is credited against the meals carried.

## 3. Stored value

No account is taken of the stored value the employee already holds. The stored value taken into account is never moved from the account: it stays spendable, the meals it will meet are never charged to payroll, and that is why the charge carried is net of it.

## 4. Charges already accrued

Nothing is taken off for charges already accrued.

## 5. Refunds

No refund is credited against the meals carried.

## 6. Guest surcharge

No guest surcharge is added.

## 7. Assembling the figure

The charge carried to payroll is the meals carried, less the allowance credited, less the stored value taken into account, less the charges already accrued and less the refund credited, with the guest surcharge due added on top, and it is never read as less than nothing. The deductions are taken in the order written and the guest surcharge is added last, and the figure is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end.

## 8. The period it is carried in

The payroll period the charge is carried in is the period the most recent charge accrued on the account carries.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take an account whose ledger shows meals rung against payroll to date of $214.60, and which holds $55.00 of stored value.

The meals carried are $214.60. No allowance is credited, so $214.60 stands. No account is taken of the stored value, so the $55.00 on the account does not come off and stays spendable. Nothing is taken off for charges already accrued and no refund is credited, so $214.60 stands still. No guest surcharge is added. Rounded once at the end, the charge carried to the employee's pay is $214.60, and it is carried in the payroll period the most recent charge accrued on the account carries.

Where the deductions between them came to more than the meals carried, the figure would be nothing, since it is never read as less than nothing.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
